verdict: R1's central finding (Imunify360 actively gating catalog + API) is NOT REPRODUCIBLE from the R2 audit IP and is contradicted by live production crawler state (4281 products tracked, 12 consecutive successful crawl-verify events 2026-05-12, zero errorMessages, zero consecutiveFailures). R1 was either (a) probing from an IP that Imunify had transiently rate-limit-flagged, (b) captured a brief WAF rule-toggle window, or (c) misclassified an unrelated artifact. The DB siteProfile (hasWaf=false, needsPlaywright=false) matches the live R2 observation. Most R1 corrections to DB are REJECTED.

corrections.why: R2 ran 4 user-agents (desktop Chrome, curl/8.0.0, blank UA, HeadlessChrome) against /shop/ + /wp-json/wp/v2/product?per_page=1 + 10-page rapid burst on /shop/page/{1..10}/ + 20-hit burst on /wp-json/wp/v2/product?page={1..20} -- ALL returned HTTP 200, server=LiteSpeed (NOT openresty/1.29.x), title 'Shop - Surplus GNG', 24 WC product cards on /shop/, and real JSON on the WP REST API. Zero occurrences of R1's claimed markers 'f03s36su46c0' / 'One moment, please' / '/z[0-9a-f]{40}' / 'openresty' across all responses. DB siteProfile.hasWaf=false matches R2 observation.
No Imunify360 challenge observed by R2. See hasWaf justification.

Plain axios/curl returns full /shop/ HTML (121KB, 24 products in WC markup) and full WP REST JSON. Stealth Playwright produces IDENTICAL output (200, 24 products, 525ms). Playwright fallback is unnecessary. Production crawler has run 12 consecutive successful crawl-verify in maintain phase WITHOUT Playwright -- proof at scale.
Method is fine; the recorded RESULT in wafProbeEvidence.imunify360Challenge is the problem. R2 cannot reproduce R1's evidence string with any of 4 UAs and a 20-hit burst from R2 IP.

skillGapsReassessed.r2Stance: Valid future-proofing -- Imunify360 IS a real WAF. Even though this site is not currently using it, adding it to the enum is harmless. However, the markers R1 lists (openresty/1.29 + 'One moment, please...' + '/z[0-9a-f]{40}') ARE the documented Imunify360 anti-bot challenge fingerprint -- R1's detection rule is correct; only R1's claim that THIS SITE uses Imunify is wrong.

skillGapsReassessed.r1Gap: wp-rest-header arm has no Playwright fallback when hasWaf=true
skillGapsReassessed.r2Stance: Valid concern in general, but does NOT apply to this site. Worth filing as a SKILL.md improvement for future Imunify-fronted WordPress sites.

skillGapsReassessed.r1Gap: BATCH 1 of heavy-8-batch probe misses catalog-path-only WAFs (probes /, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml; not /shop/)
skillGapsReassessed.r2Stance: Valid in principle -- some WAFs do challenge only catalog paths. But this gap did NOT cause the R1 misfire on this site: R1 DID probe /shop/ (and reported it as challenged); the issue was that R1's /shop/ probe returned an Imunify-looking response that R2 cannot reproduce. Recommend SKILL.md addendum: 'When BATCH 1 says no-WAF but BATCH 4 catalog-paths show challenge, re-probe BATCH 4 from a second IP / second time window before promoting hasWaf=true to DB.'
